tuple: (two playbooks match one trigger, run neither; clarification.request naming both)
why: The product runtime has no playbook-matching engine: agents act on intents, and no component picks a playbook for a trigger, so two matches cannot be detected.

tuple: (a playbook step conflicts with an agent's legal line, halt playbook; integrity.violation - spec defect, never a judgment call)
why: No component compares a playbook step with an agent's legal lines; phase gates re-inject MANNERS.md but check nothing against the step.

tuple: (workload exceeds capacity, priority order: escalations > active-transaction deadlines > client-facing requests > internal/marketing > discovery; ties go to the older item)
why: dispatcher/priority.py (SidingScheduler) implements the priority classes and is tested in the dispatcher-agents core repo (tests/test_day3.py), but the product runtime never creates one; envelopes are handled in arrival order.

tuple: (signed human instruction conflicts with a playbook, signed human wins; deviation logged in the after-action report)
why: Signed human decisions do win everywhere they are taken (release, decline, decide, signed settings), but dispatcher/after_action.py is not called by the product runtime, so no deviation is written to an after-action report.

tuple: (required data is stale beyond threshold, regenerate; never present stale as current)
note: Agent 10's staleness check (30 days): the stale comp is left out and counted, and the package is built fresh per request.

tuple: (one parallel step fails mid-phase, complete independent siblings; hold dependents; flag - never abandon the phase silently)
note: One step (filing into the client drawer) fails: it is flagged and held, and the independent steps (capture, scoring, CRM log) still complete.

tuple: (identical envelope arrives twice, process once; envelope_id is the idempotency key)
note: Harness: one envelope (one envelope_id) sent twice. The second is answered as a duplicate and processed nothing.

tuple: (uncertainty about whether a legal line is crossed, treat as crossed; escalate)
note: Agent 08 cannot tell whether the sender of a sensitive document is legitimate (no sender list), so it treats it as crossed: quarantined and escalated, nothing moves the closing.

tuple: (no suitable tuple exists for the task at hand, STOP; clarification.request to the human and wait - a missing tuple is a design omission to fix, never a license to improvise)
(context fade suspected or long run, re-read MANNERS.md and own SKILL.md before the next action)
note: Every phase gate (listing intake, go-live) re-injects MANNERS.md; a turn backstop fires after N turns with no other re-injection.

tuple: (visibility limited but the path seems clear, proceed only within stopping distance: reversible increments; irreversible or client-visible actions wait for full verified authority)
note: Client- and counterparty-visible actions (the photographer booking, the ad) are held until the broker signs the release.

tuple: (two runs contend for the same agent, higher priority class proceeds; the lower takes the siding - held live on route, resumes when the segment clears; contention never aborts a run)
why: Siding (held live, resumes when the segment clears) is implemented in dispatcher/priority.py and tested in the dispatcher-agents core repo (tests/test_day3.py), but the product runtime never creates a SidingScheduler.

tuple: (task requires a path outside declared edges, refuse; clarification.request - an undeclared path is ambiguity, not opportunity)
note: Stand-in: an agent sends on an edge routes.json does not declare (06 -> 14 record.request); the hub refuses it before delivery.

tuple: (an unlisted crossing is reached, ambiguity protocol; propose the missing tuple in the after-action report for human ratification)
why: The ambiguity protocol runs (checked below: a client reply routed to Agent 12, which has no tuple for it, is held for the broker). The second half, proposing the missing tuple in an after-action report, has no runtime: after_action.py is not called by the product.
